headlines.article_text: Anthropic stock sinks below $83 IPO price Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Anthropic stock sank on Tuesday, falling below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price. Shares of ANT have been sinking steadily since the stock opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq. Analysts are still bullish about the company, citing its potential to capture a large addressable market. In this article ANT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Dario Amodei, chief executive officer of Anthropic PBC, speaks during the company's initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Shares of Anthropic fell 8% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price. The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time. Investors eagerly awaited Anthropic's debut in hopes that the company would revitalize the broader AI trade, which has been volatile in recent weeks over concerns about the feasibility of a multi-trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout. Anthropic's IPO was oversubscribed, and roughly half of the institutional investors that placed orders for the stock were left empty-handed, as CNBC previously reported . But at least for now, as the market wavers, those firms don't appear to be racing to scoop up shares. Chip stocks Nvidia , Advanced Micro Devices and Intel , as well as neoclouds CoreWeave , IREN and Nebius , all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday. The market is still reeling after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a dramatic reversal from his ouster earlier this month. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday, but pared those gains Tuesday. Analysts at Canaccord Genuity said Tuesday that they're focused on Anthropic's long-term potential. They said they believe the company is building "one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era" and that the "opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending." Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target. "The risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation, but we believe the combination of exceptional growth, emerging earnings capacity, and an attractive entry valuation support a compelling investment opportunity," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note. They said Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" as debate around the AI buildout continues, but that they expect the company to navigate the competitive environment and "capture a uniquely large addressable market." "While there's going to continue to be many ups and downs, and winners and losers as this ecosystem gets built, in our view there is no real question that it does get built over time," the analysts wrote in a Monday note. "The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme." Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock. They said their "bullish stance" on the company stems from their belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending, that its improving compute efficiency lowers cost per task and that its multi-chip strategy optimizes price-performance. The analysts added that Anthropic's focus on the enterprise also relies less on consumer subsidies, and that rising customer adoption creates "a substantial runway" for the company. "While competition and compute commitments remain risks, we believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note. headlines.article_text: Best Buy (BBY) Q3 2027 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Best Buy beat quarterly expectations for its fiscal third-quarter earnings results on Tuesday and raised its full-year guidance. The company reported comparable sales growth of 6.1%, beating StreetAccount estimates of 2.3%. It's Best Buy's first earnings report under CEO Jason Bonfig, who recently took over the reins of the consumer electronics retailer. In this article BBY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A Grand Theft Auto VI advertisement is displayed at a Best Buy store at the Atlantic Terminal Mall on Nov. 19, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images Best Buy on Tuesday beat Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines for its third fiscal quarter and raised its full-year guidance. The consumer electronics retailer reported comparable sales growth of 6.1%, a significant beat over expectations of 2.3%, according to market intelligence platform StreetAccount. The company said that growth was its highest in five years. It reported a domestic comparable sales increase of 6.2% and international comparable sales growth of 4.9%. "We have a tremendous amount of momentum," CEO Jason Bonfig told CNBC. "The fact that we saw pretty much broad-based growth across almost all of our categories is a lot of momentum that we're very excited about." Best Buy also raised its guidance for the rest of the year. It's now expecting full-year revenue of between $43 billion and $43.3 billion compared with a previous expectation of between $42.3 billion and $42.8 billion. It's expecting comparable sales to be up 3.4% to 4% compared with prior guidance of between 1.9% and 3%. The earnings report is the company's first since Bonfig took over as CEO from Corie Barry at the beginning of the month. Bonfig said the retailer saw overperformance in both computing and gaming for the quarter, driven by recent game launches and a targeted product assortment. Looking ahead into the holiday season, he said the Best Buy consumer remains "resilient," but that they are focused on getting value wherever they can. "We did see not only our current customers continue to be engaged, but we actually did see more new customers come into the brand, as well as we had some customers that we re-engaged as well," Bonfig said. "So those are really, really positive signs for us in Q3, and all of that was factored into the way that we guided for Q4 and the rest of the year." Here's how the company performed in the period ended Oct. 31 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.62 adjusted vs. $1.49 expected Revenue: $10.24 billion vs. $9.90 billion expected Best Buy reported net income of $353 million, or $1.66 per share, compared with $140 million, or 66 cents per share, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time items, including restructuring charges, Best Buy posted adjusted earnings of $1.62 per share. Revenue rose to $10.24 billion from $9.67 billion in the year-ago period. Best Buy reported domestic revenue of $9.42 billion and international revenue of $820 million. Tuesday's earnings are the latest in a series of strong reports from the retailer, which has been instituting a turnaround strategy to return to growth after getting hit by declining foot traffic, lower consumer sentiment, tariffs and memory costs . Shares of Best Buy are up nearly 45% this year. Bonfig told CNBC last quarter that the launch of " Grand Theft Auto VI " in the current quarter is expected to drive sales in the gaming category, which has been seeing gains over the past year. Last month, Best Buy launched a new gaming experience for customers featuring gaming content, technology and special offers, among other features. "I think there'll still be opportunities for gaming to continue to drive our business moving forward," Bonfig told CNBC on Tuesday. headlines.article_text: Signal joins United Airlines, banks in limiting AI agents Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Privacy-focused Signal says AI agents built into mobile operating systems can scan information on users' screens, potentially capturing and storing Signal data outside its control. Signal called on Apple, Google and Microsoft to provide simple technical tools and documentation that let developers prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data. The move follows restrictions by companies including United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab, which have limited or blocked AI agents over security and customer-protection concerns. Jakub Porzycki | Nurphoto | Getty Images Privacy-focused messaging application Signal is tightening protections against artificial intelligence agents that can access information displayed on users' screens, citing concerns over privacy and security. Signal said AI agents built into mobile operating systems, such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri with onscreen awareness, can "scan" information on users' screens, potentially capturing and storing Signal data outside its control. People treat agent risk as one-size-fits-all rather than matching the security needed to the actual task. Yat Siu Co-founder, Animoca Brands The company said it will block screenshots in its iOS app and, on Android, enable screen security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to read the screen. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal — and application developers beyond — lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," Meredith Whittaker, president of the app's nonprofit parent Signal Foundation, said in a Friday blog post . Signal last year introduced similar restrictions against Microsoft's Recall AI on Windows 11. Its latest move adds to a broader push by companies including United Airlines , JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab to limit or block AI agents over security and for customer-protection concerns. Whittaker said the new protections do not address every way an agent might gain access to data, including by retrieving content already stored on a user's device. Signal also warned that third-party agents such as Meta's Muse could gain access to private app content through permissions granted during setup. "Application-level protections will always have gaps, so the data an agent can reach has to be classified, permissioned and recoverable before the agent arrives," said Tianyi Jiang, CEO of data management and protection software company AvePoint. AvePoint's State of AI 2026 report found that 88.4% of surveyed organizations had experienced at least one AI-agent-related security breach in the previous year. The survey covered 750 IT leaders globally. "We continue to call on the major consumer operating system companies – Apple, Google and Microsoft – to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation that give developers like Signal ways to prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data," said Whittaker. Restricted entry Banks are also restricting third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said in October that outside agents were too risky for the bank and its clients. Morgan Stanley has blocked third-party agents from its platforms, Reuters reported. Meanwhile, Charles Schwab CEO Richard Wurster said the brokerage blocks unauthorized agents to protect clients and the firm. Singapore's OCBC Bank has said it will not let third-party agents to interact with the bank to transfer money autonomously and warned that "customers should exercise caution" when using such agents for banking. United Airlines said Nov. 11 that it would restrict unauthorized agents from booking or managing tickets, citing risks that they could expose customer information, make unintended purchases or violate aviation rules. "To book flights or do your grocery shop, an agent needs your email, accounts and payment details," said Mick Amelishko, an AI advocate at identity verification and compliance platform Sumsub. He said that level of access creates a risk of account hijacking because actions taken by an agent may appear to a retailer or bank to have been authorized by the user. Singapore Airlines , by contrast, is an early partner of Meta's Muse. Meta said users can ask the agent to explore travel, ticketing and reservation options through the airline. "People treat agent risk as one-size-fits-all rather than matching the security needed to the actual task," said Yat Siu, executive chairman and co-founder of Animoca Brands. He said agents could help consumers act on their intentions and help businesses reach customers directly, but the risks vary by task. "There's a much higher risk around an agent able to move meaningful sums of money or access sensitive personal data, than one making your restaurant reservations," Siu said. "The reality is that, just like internet applications to date, agents require tiered safeguards." The acquisition includes Insmed's portfolio of two commercialized respiratory drugs as well as its pipeline of experimental candidates. Sanofi will pay $175 per share in cash. It's a big bet by new Sanofi CEO Belen Garijo, who took up the role in May to steer the company through its upcoming patent cliff , when its blockbuster immunology drug Dupixent will face generic competition as patents expire. If closed, the transaction will be the biggest one the industry has seen since Pfizer bought Seagen for $43 billion in December 2023. Insmed shares rose 14.3% to roughly $170.40 in morning trading, while Sanofi stock rose 8% in Paris. 'Buys time' Barclays analysts called the deal a "breath of fresh air," significantly improving Sanofi's Dupixent patent expiry outlook by adding Insmed's established respiratory assets Brinsupri and Arikayce, plus a late-stage pipeline offering further potential upside. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and be accretive to earnings by the end of 2028, Sanofi said. Like much of the industry, Sanofi faces a revenue drop towards the end of the decade as top-selling drugs lose exclusivity and open up for generic drugmakers to compete. Global biopharma has experienced a sharp uptick in deals in 2026 , as the sector is driven by looming patent cliffs, newly buoyant public markets, and a race to beef up pipelines. Following a post-pandemic trough in 2022, M&A activity surged in 2025 and has accelerated into 2026. While companies develop new medicines in-house, acquiring them is often faster and has become the go-to strategy for large biopharma companies with strong cash flows and financial firepower. Investors are also calling for sustainable revenue growth as major drugs lose exclusivity. Sanofi/Insmed shares over the past 12 months. "Sanofi could offer a far more attractive investment opportunity given the significantly improved growth outlook," Barclays said in a note early Tuesday. Formerly CEO at Merck KGaA , Garijo is facing pressure to find Sanofi's next growth driver. Her predecessor Paul Hudson stepped down earlier this year after the board chose not to renew his mandate , following a six-year reign during which his costly emphasis on R&D failed to deliver speedy results.
